 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J.
1. Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Satya Narayan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ashutosh Singh,
learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.318 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 DP Act, Police Station Chopan,
District Sonbhadra, during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and his first bail application has been dismissed by Hon?ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J. but as his Lordship has already been transferred and this Bench is dealing with such matters, therefore, the instant matter has been listed today for hearing before this Bench.
5.

He next submits, however applicant is husband of the deceased but he is in jail since 28.03.2022 i.e. for last almost four years and therefore, he has already served more than half of the minimum sentence provided under Section 304-B IPC.
6.
He also submits, in the charge-sheet there are 25 prosecution witnesses but till date only 6 witnesses could be examined, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of trial.
7. He also argued, even from the post mortem report of the deceased it appears, she committed suicide.
8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and his first bail application has been dismissed by Hon?ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J. but as his Lordship has already been transferred and this Bench is dealing with such matters, therefore, the instant matter has been listed for hearing before this Bench.

11. Although applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstance in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of torture in connection with demand of dowry but considering the post mortem report of the deceased prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death and applicant is in jail for last three and half years, therefore, he has already served more than half of the minimum sentence provided under Section 304B IPC.

sentences.text: Further, in the charge-sheet there are as many as 25 witnesses and till date only 6 witnesses could be examined, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of the trial and there is no material on record, which can sugges that applicant is responsible for delay in trial.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant - Vinod Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
(Sameer Jain,J.) January 6, 2026 S.A.
